Install Bun and Node, then from the repository root:\n\n```sh\nbun install --cwd js --frozen-lockfile\nbun run --cwd js format:check\nbun run --cwd js lint\nbun run --cwd js build\nbun test js/tests\nbun scripts/ci/check-js-gate.mjs\nbun test experiments/issue-339/ci-contract.test.mjs\nnode scripts/ci/check-parity.mjs\nnode --test experiments/issue-339/parity-contract.test.mjs experiments/issue-339/release-audit.test.mjs\npython3 experiments/issue-339/test_workflow_contract.py\nnode scripts/version-consistency.mjs\nnode scripts/ci/php-distribution.mjs\nnode --test experiments/issue-339/php-distribution.test.mjs\npython3 experiments/issue-332/test_test_comparison.py\nnode scripts/create-test-case-comparison.mjs --check\n```\n\nAfter reviewing feature coverage, run\n`node scripts/ci/check-parity.mjs --refresh-inventory`. Commit the manifest and\ngenerated text vectors together. Hashes require an inventory review when code\nchanges; the native tests validate behavior. Refreshing hashes alone does not\nestablish parity.\n\nFor native checks use the commands in the reusable workflows: `pytest` and\nBlack/isort/flake8 for Python, `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` for Go,\n`./mvnw test`, `bash format.sh --check` and `./mvnw spotless:check` for Java,\n`dotnet test --configuration Release` and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`\nfor C#, `composer run-script test` / `lint` for PHP, and\n`cmake -S cpp -B build && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build` plus\n`clang-format --dry-run --Werror` (version pinned in `cpp/tools/requirements.txt`)\nfor C++, and `./gradlew ktlintCheck jvmTest jsNodeTest wasmJsNodeTest` from\n`kotlin/` for Kotlin (`iosSimulatorArm64Test` needs macOS and\n`testAndroidHostTest` an Android SDK; CI runs both). PHP distribution changes\nalso require `python3 experiments/issue-339/test_php_distribution.py` from the\nroot, using PHP 8.4+ and Composer. Refresh root metadata after changing\n`php/composer.json` with `node scripts/ci/php-distribution.mjs --write`.\nWorkflow changes also\nrequire actionlint with shellcheck on PATH, `shellcheck -x scripts/ci/*.sh`,\n`bash scripts/ci/registry-probe.test.sh`, and the zizmor command in\n`.github/workflows/workflows.yml`. After adding tests, regenerate the comparison\nwith `node scripts/create-test-case-comparison.mjs`. After a library version bump,\nregenerate benchmarks with `cargo run -p links-notation-benchmark --release`\nfrom `rust/`, using the bounded Rust settings below. Check the result with\n`cargo run -p links-notation-benchmark --release -- --check`. Save verbose logs\nin `ci-logs/`.\n\nFor Rust use one shared, bounded build directory rather than a separate target\ntree per agent:\n\n```sh\nexport CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"/tmp/links-notation-cargo\"\nexport CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2\nexport CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0\nbash scripts/ci/check-rust-target-budget.sh\ncargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace\ncargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p links-notation --no-default-features\ncargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features \\\n  -- -D warnings\nbash scripts/ci/check-rust-target-budget.sh\n```\n\nThe budget check defaults to 2 GiB and fails when exceeded. Stop all users of\nthe shared directory before explicitly cleaning build output. Do not run\nsimultaneous Rust builds in that directory. Deliberate stack/memory probes must\nuse finite inputs and process limits; preserve their scripts in `experiments/`.\n\n## One push gate\n\nWhen using sub-agents, drafting agents edit, test, and make useful local\ncommits; they never push, merge, or deploy. One designated CI/CD agent owns\npushing the PR branch. It collects every failure from the latest commit's\ncompleted runs, downloads their logs, fixes the complete failure set, runs local\nchecks, and pushes once. No agent pushes while a run for that branch/range is in\nprogress. Keep history forward-moving; do not rewrite the shared branch.\n\nBefore a push, inspect `gh pr checks` and the recent runs:\n\n```sh\ngh run list --repo link-foundation/links-notation --branch BRANCH --limit 5 \\\n  --json databaseId,status,conclusion,createdAt,headSha\n```\n\nMatch runs to the latest SHA and timestamp. Save non-passing\nlogs using `gh run view RUN --log` under `ci-logs/`, inspect actual errors, and\nwait for all running jobs and delegated work. Repeat only after the next run\nfinishes. GitHub's concurrency setting preserves active runs; it can replace an\nolder pending run, so it does not replace this push rule.\n\n## CI and releases\n\n`.github/workflows/js.yml` is the single CI entry point. It calls\n`javascript.yml` from the same commit, then the nine other language workflows,\nbinary interop, security, benchmarks, and docs. JS format/lint/test/parity always run\nfor every PR and main push. Cancelled, failed, or skipped JS prevents non-JS\nexecution. [2026-11-02T17:00:54.133Z] [INFO]         "content": "| C/C++                 | clang-tidy + cppcheck (warnings as errors) |\n| PHP                   | PHPStan (max level)                        |\n\n### 5. Fast-Fail Job Ordering\n\n**Run fast checks before slow checks** to give the fastest possible feedback:\n\n```\nFast checks (~7-30s each):     Slow checks (~1-10 min each):\n├── test-compilation            ├── test-suites (unit tests)\n├── lint (format + ESLint)      ├── test-execution (integration)\n└── check-file-line-limits      ├── docker-pr-check\n                                └── helm-pr-check\n```\n\nGate slow checks on fast checks:\n\n```yaml\ntest-suites:\n  needs: [test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]\n  if: |\n    always() &&\n    !cancelled() &&\n    !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&\n    needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' &&\n    needs.lint.result == 'success' &&\n    needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success'\n```\n\n### 6. Changeset-Based Versioning\n\n  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n  steps:\n    - name: Check for version changes in package.json\n      run: node scripts/check-version.mjs\n```\n\n### 10. Concurrency Control\n\n**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:\n\n```yaml\njobs:\n  lint:\n    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated\n    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.\n    concurrency:\n      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-lint\n      cancel-in-progress: true\n    # ...\n\n  deploy:\n    needs: [lint]\n    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}\n    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this\n    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.\n    concurrency:\n      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main\n      cancel-in-progress: false\n    # ...\n```\n\n- **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded checks on both pull requests and `main` to reduce runner load. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.\n- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.\n- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.\n- **Workflow scope:** Do not put cancellable concurrency at workflow level when the workflow has write jobs. Cancelling the workflow would also interrupt a writer that has already started.\n\nBy default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.\n\nUse `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.\n\n**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:\n\n```\n ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)\n```\n\nThe bullets above without this one convert \"two writers collide\" into \"the second writer reliably fails\" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.\n\n**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.\n\n**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — \"Changes must be made through a pull request\") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.\n\n```js\nfor (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {\n  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);\n  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };\n  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.\n  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });\n  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.\n  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);\n  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);\n}\n```\n\n- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.\n- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.\n- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.\n- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.\n\n### 11. Secrets Detection\n\n- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.\n- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.\n- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.\n\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n\n## Quality Enforcement Strategy\n\nThe templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:\n\n```\nDeveloper Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release\n├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass\n├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump\n└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update\n                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package\n                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)\n                          ├── check-file-line-limits\n                          ├── test-suites\n                          ├── test-execution\n                          ├── validate-docs\n                          └── docker-pr-check\n```\n\nEach layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.",

Fast-Fail Job Ordering\n\n**Run fast checks before slow checks** to give the fastest possible feedback:\n\n```\nFast checks (~7-30s each):     Slow checks (~1-10 min each):\n├── test-compilation            ├── test-suites (unit tests)\n├── lint (format + ESLint)      ├── test-execution (integration)\n└── check-file-line-limits      ├── docker-pr-check\n                                └── helm-pr-check\n```\n\nGate slow checks on fast checks:\n\n```yaml\ntest-suites:\n  needs: [test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]\n  if: |\n    always() &&\n    !cancelled() &&\n    !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&\n    needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' &&\n    needs.lint.result == 'success' &&\n    needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success'\n```\n\n### 6. Concurrency Control\n\n**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:\n\n```yaml\njobs:\n  lint:\n    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated\n    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.\n    concurrency:\n      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-lint\n      cancel-in-progress: true\n    # ...\n\n  deploy:\n    needs: [lint]\n    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}\n    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this\n    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.\n    concurrency:\n      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main\n      cancel-in-progress: false\n    # ...\n```\n\n- **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded checks on both pull requests and `main` to reduce runner load. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.\n- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.\n- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.\n- **Workflow scope:** Do not put cancellable concurrency at workflow level when the workflow has write jobs. Cancelling the workflow would also interrupt a writer that has already started.\n\nBy default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.\n\nUse `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.\n\n**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:\n\n```\n ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)\n```\n\nThe bullets above without this one convert \"two writers collide\" into \"the second writer reliably fails\" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.\n\n**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.\n\n**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — \"Changes must be made through a pull request\") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.\n\n```js\nfor (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {\n  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);\n  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };\n  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.\n  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });\n  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.\n  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);\n  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);\n}\n```\n\n- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.\n- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. [2026-11-02T17:04:08.815Z] [INFO]         "content": "### 10. Concurrency Control\n\n**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:\n\n```yaml\njobs:\n  lint:\n    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated\n    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.\n    concurrency:\n      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-lint\n      cancel-in-progress: true\n    # ...\n\n  deploy:\n    needs: [lint]\n    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}\n    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this\n    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.\n    concurrency:\n      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main\n      cancel-in-progress: false\n    # ...\n```\n\n- **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded checks on both pull requests and `main` to reduce runner load. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.\n- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.\n- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.\n- **Workflow scope:** Do not put cancellable concurrency at workflow level when the workflow has write jobs. Cancelling the workflow would also interrupt a writer that has already started.\n\nBy default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.\n\nUse `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.\n\n**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:\n\n```\n ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)\n```\n\nThe bullets above without this one convert \"two writers collide\" into \"the second writer reliably fails\" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.\n\n**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.\n\n**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — \"Changes must be made through a pull request\") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.\n\n```js\nfor (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {\n  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);\n  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };\n  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.\n  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });\n  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.\n  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);\n  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);\n}\n```\n\n- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.\n- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.\n- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.\n- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.\n\n### 11. Secrets Detection\n\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n\n## Quality Enforcement Strategy",

The person who has to debug it has no reason to look at a release commit.\n\n## Reproducing it\n\nNo exotic setup is needed — the mechanism is a documented platform rule plus an ordering:\n\n```console\n$ gh run list --commit \"$(git log --format='%H %an' origin/main | awk '$2==\"github-actions[bot]\"{print $1; exit}')\"\n[]\n```\n\nAny release commit in any repository built from these templates will print an empty list. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. JS is the reference implementation (js/src/comments.js, js/src/StreamParser.js `structurallyComplete`, js/src/Cst.js, js/src/grammar.pegjs, js/src/quotes.js, js/src/ReferenceLiteral.js `referenceLiteralEnd`).\n\nThree bugs (issue #377), each must be fixed in every binding:\n1. **Comment pre-pass misses reference starts.** The comment stripper (blanks `#...` comments to spaces, keeping positions) decided whether a quote opens a delimited reference by looking at the previous character (`BEFORE_REFERENCE = space, tab, \\n, \\r, (, :`). But the grammar lets a reference start at any token start: after a separator (space, tab, \\n, \\r, `(`, `:`, `)`), and also immediately after a delimited (quoted) reference or a versioned literal `~<digits>{<payload>}` (payload excludes `}`, space, tab, \\r, \\n, `(`, `)`). Fix: scan token by token with a `tokenStart` flag: a `#` at the start of the document or after space/tab/\\n/\\r opens a comment (blank it to the line end, unchanged rule); a separator sets tokenStart=true; at a token start try a versioned literal end, then (if the char is a quote `\"`, `'`, `` ` ``) a delimited reference end — if one is read, jump past it and stay at a token start; otherwise tokenStart=false and advance one char. An unreadable quote at a token start is just a bare-reference character.\n2. **References read from the blanked text.** The parser/grammar and the CST builder read delimited references from the comment-blanked document. Blanking a comment can flip whether an even-run body is \"substantive\" (has a visible char and balanced parens) or remove a closing run, so the value changes. Fix: read delimited references (and literals) from the source document as written (same positions), keep bare-token ends in the blanked document. In hand-written parsers that slice the blanked text, read from the source at the same absolute offsets bounded to the slice extent (see how Python's parser.py `_quoted_at` does it with a `stop` bound on `_parse_quoted_string_at`). Look for where each port builds its delimited-reference reader/cache from `prepared`, and switch it to the source input.\n3. **Stream parser emits too early.** The stream parser's structural-completeness check must follow the same token model (separators incl. `)` with paren depth counting, tokenStart flag, quote at token start → if unreadable return false, literal skipping) AND must return false when a quote run at a token start has no closing run anywhere later in the buffer (an even run nothing closes reads as the empty reference, but a later line can close it: whole-document parse of `a \"\" b\\n\"\" c\\n` is one link `(a ' b\\n' c)`, while the stream used to emit `(a '' b)` then `('' c)`).\n\n## Evidence / tests\n- Shared fixtures in parity/syntax-fixtures.json already include 5 new rows (ids comment-after-group-quote, comment-after-adjacent-quote, comment-after-literal-quote, comment-after-empty-quote, stream-empty-quote-closed-later); parity/syntax-vectors.tsv is regenerated. Reading a reference takes time\n * linear in its body however wide its opening run is, and finding that a\n * reference never closes does not take a pass over the rest of the document\n * each time it is asked.\n */\n\n/** The characters a reference can be written between. */\nexport const QUOTES = ['\"', \"'\", '`'];\n\n/**\n * Every delimited reference of one document, read on demand.\n *\n * The grammar and the comment reader each keep one per document they read, so\n * a reference asked for twice is read once.\n */\nexport class DelimitedReferences {\n  /**\n   * @param {string} document - The document the references are read from\n   */\n  constructor(document) {\n    this.document = document;\n    this.runsByQuote = new Map();\n    this.readings = new Map();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The reference opened at `start`.\n   * @param {number} start - Position of the opening delimiter\n   * @returns {{value: string, length: number, closed: boolean}|null} What the\n   *   reference holds, how many characters it takes and whether a run closes\n   *   it (an even run nothing closes is the empty reference, until a closing\n   *   run is written after it), or null when nothing opens there\n   */\n  readAt(start) {\n    if (!this.readings.has(start)) {\n      this.readings.set(start, this.#read(start));\n    }\n    return this.readings.get(start);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * The position just past the reference opened at `start`.\n   * @param {number} start - Position of the opening delimiter\n   * @returns {number|null} The position, or null when nothing opens there\n   */\n  endAt(start) {\n    const reading = this.readAt(start);\n    return reading === null ? References are read in the document as written, as the grammar\n * reads them.\n * @param {string} document - The document to read\n * @returns {string} The document, of the same length, without its comments\n * @example\n * stripComments('a: b # why\\n'); // 'a: b      \\n'\n * stripComments('\"# kept\"\\n'); // '\"# kept\"\\n'\n * stripComments('(a)\" #kept\"\\n'); // '(a)\" #kept\"\\n'\n * stripComments('issue#1047\\n'); // 'issue#1047\\n'\n */\nexport function stripComments(document) {\n  // Split into UTF-16 units, the units the positions here and the positions a\n  // parse error reports are both counted in.\n  let blanked = null;\n  let position = 0;\n  // Whether a token may start at `position`.\n  let tokenStart = true;\n  const references = new DelimitedReferences(document);\n\n  while (position < document.length) {\n    const character = document[position];\n\n    if (character === COMMENT && follows(document, position, BEFORE_COMMENT)) {\n      blanked = blanked ?? document : blanked.join('');\n}\n\n/**\n * The position just past the delimited reference or versioned literal that\n * starts the token at `start`, or `null` when the token there is a bare\n * reference: a delimiter run that never closes is read as one, as the grammar\n * reads it.\n * @param {string} document - The document being read\n * @param {number} start - Position where a token starts\n * @param {DelimitedReferences} references - The references of the document\n * @returns {number|null} The position just past the token\n */\nexport function delimitedTokenEnd(document, start, references) {\n  const literal = referenceLiteralEnd(document, start);\n  if (literal !== -1) {\n    return literal;\n  }\n  return QUOTES.includes(document[start]) ? references.endAt(start) : null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the character before the given position is one the caller allows,\n * the start of the document counting as allowed.\n * @param {string} document - The document being read\n * @param {number} position - Position of the character being judged\n * @param {string[]} allowed - The characters that may stand before it\n * @returns {boolean} True when the position opens a token\n */\nfunction follows(document, position, allowed) {\n  return position === 0 || allowed.includes(document[position - 1]);\n}\n\n/**\n * The position just past the delimited reference that starts at `start`, or\n * `null` when nothing there opens one.\n *\n * This follows the same rules as the `parseQuotedStringAt` of the grammar: a\n * run of N delimiters closes at the next run of exactly N, a run of 2N is that\n * delimiter escaped, and an even run that encloses nothing substantive is the\n * empty reference.\n * @param {string} document - The document being read\n * @param {number} start - Position of the opening delimiter\n * @returns {number|null} The position just past the reference\n */\nexport function quotedReferenceEnd(document, start) {\n  const reading = readReference(document, start);\n  return reading === null ? Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md first.\n\n## The fix (already done in JS and Python — use them as the reference)\nRead these commits with `git show`: b41fd15 (JS main fix), a875202 (JS stream fix), 3b3efc4 (Python port). JS is the reference implementation (js/src/comments.js, js/src/StreamParser.js `structurallyComplete`, js/src/Cst.js, js/src/grammar.pegjs, js/src/quotes.js, js/src/ReferenceLiteral.js `referenceLiteralEnd`).\n\nThree bugs (issue #377), each must be fixed in every binding:\n1. **Comment pre-pass misses reference starts.** The comment stripper (blanks `#...` comments to spaces, keeping positions) decided whether a quote opens a delimited reference by looking at the previous character (`BEFORE_REFERENCE = space, tab, \\n, \\r, (, :`). But the grammar lets a reference start at any token start: after a separator (space, tab, \\n, \\r, `(`, `:`, `)`), and also immediately after a delimited (quoted) reference or a versioned literal `~<digits>{<payload>}` (payload excludes `}`, space, tab, \\r, \\n, `(`, `)`). Fix: scan token by token with a `tokenStart` flag: a `#` at the start of the document or after space/tab/\\n/\\r opens a comment (blank it to the line end, unchanged rule); a separator sets tokenStart=true; at a token start try a versioned literal end, then (if the char is a quote `\"`, `'`, `` ` ``) a delimited reference end — if one is read, jump past it and stay at a token start; otherwise tokenStart=false and advance one char. An unreadable quote at a token start is just a bare-reference character.\n2. **References read from the blanked text.** The parser/grammar and the CST builder read delimited references from the comment-blanked document. Blanking a comment can flip whether an even-run body is \"substantive\" (has a visible char and balanced parens) or remove a closing run, so the value changes. Fix: read delimited references (and literals) from the source document as written (same positions), keep bare-token ends in the blanked document. Known spots from an earlier survey (verify): rust/links-notation/src/cst.rs ~311 `DelimitedReferences::new(prepared)` → source; rust parser.rs ~414 and ~786 `DelimitedReferences::new(input)` (check whether `input` is the blanked text there; lib.rs ~1016 does the stripping); kotlin Cst.kt ~206 (prepared → source) and Grammar.kt ~36 `DelimitedReferences(input)`; swift Cst.swift ~140 and Grammar.swift ~73; swift `stripComments` lives in Swift Sources/LinksNotation/Quotes.swift ~190, StreamParser.swift ~370; kotlin StreamParser.kt ~263; rust stream_parser.rs ~522; cpp comments.cpp, stream_parser.cpp, cst.cpp ~89, parser.cpp ~661.\n3. **Stream parser emits too early.** The stream parser's structural-completeness check must follow the same token model (separators incl. `)` with paren depth counting, tokenStart flag, quote at token start → if unreadable return false, literal skipping) AND must return false when a quote run at a token start has no closing run anywhere later in the buffer (an even run nothing closes reads as the empty reference, but a later line can close it: whole-document parse of `a \"\" b\\n\"\" c\\n` is one link `(a ' b\\n' c)`, while the stream used to emit `(a '' b)` then `('' c)`). But the grammar lets a reference start at any token start: after a separator (space, tab, \\n, \\r, `(`, `:`, `)`), and also immediately after a delimited (quoted) reference or a versioned literal `~<digits>{<payload>}` (payload excludes `}`, space, tab, \\r, \\n, `(`, `)`). Fix: scan token by token with a `tokenStart` flag: a `#` at the start of the document or after space/tab/\\n/\\r opens a comment (blank it to the line end, unchanged rule); a separator sets tokenStart=true; at a token start try a versioned literal end, then (if the char is a quote `\"`, `'`, `` ` ``) a delimited reference end — if one is read, jump past it and stay at a token start; otherwise tokenStart=false and advance one char. An unreadable quote at a token start is just a bare-reference character.\n2. **References read from the blanked text.** The parser/grammar and the CST builder read delimited references from the comment-blanked document. Blanking a comment can flip whether an even-run body is \"substantive\" (has a visible char and balanced parens) or remove a closing run, so the value changes. Fix: read delimited references (and literals) from the source document as written (same positions), keep bare-token ends in the blanked document. Known spots from an earlier survey (verify): rust/links-notation/src/cst.rs ~311 `DelimitedReferences::new(prepared)` → source; rust parser.rs ~414 and ~786 `DelimitedReferences::new(input)` (check whether `input` is the blanked text there; lib.rs ~1016 does the stripping); kotlin Cst.kt ~206 (prepared → source) and Grammar.kt ~36 `DelimitedReferences(input)`; swift Cst.swift ~140 and Grammar.swift ~73; swift `stripComments` lives in Swift Sources/LinksNotation/Quotes.swift ~190, StreamParser.swift ~370; kotlin StreamParser.kt ~263; rust stream_parser.rs ~522; cpp comments.cpp, stream_parser.cpp, cst.cpp ~89, parser.cpp ~661.\n3. **Stream parser emits too early.** The stream parser's structural-completeness check must follow the same token model (separators incl. `)` with paren depth counting, tokenStart flag, quote at token start → if unreadable return false, literal skipping) AND must return false when a quote run at a token start has no closing run anywhere later in the buffer (an even run nothing closes reads as the empty reference, but a later line can close it: whole-document parse of `a \"\" b\\n\"\" c\\n` is one link `(a ' b\\n' c)`, while the stream used to emit `(a '' b)` then `('' c)`). Both columns count from 1.\nfunc quoteLine(line string, column int) (string, int) {\n\tcharacters := []rune(line)\n\tif len(characters) <= quotedLineWidth {\n\t\treturn line, column\n\t}\n\n\ttarget := max(0, column-1)\n\tlastStart := len(characters) - quotedLineWidth\n\tstart := min(max(0, target-quotedLineWidth/2), lastStart)\n\tend := start + quotedLineWidth\n\n\tvar quoted strings.Builder\n\tshift := 0\n\tif start > 0 {\n\t\tquoted.WriteString(ellipsis)\n\t\tshift = len(ellipsis)\n\t}\n\tquoted.WriteString(string(characters[start:end]))\n\tif end < len(characters) {\n\t\tquoted.WriteString(ellipsis)\n\t}\n\treturn quoted.String(), target - start + shift + 1\n}\n\n// nestingTooDeep carries a ParseError out of the recursion that found it, so\n// that no caller goes on to recurse any further.\ntype nestingTooDeep struct {\n\terr *ParseError\n}\n\n// Parser for Lino notation.\ntype Parser struct {\n\tMaxInputSize int\n\n\t// MaxDepth is the deepest nesting the parser accepts. A document nested deeper is refused with a\n\t// ParseError matching ErrNestingTooDeep instead of being recursed into\n\t// until the stack is exhausted.\n\tMaxDepth int\n\n\t// Comments tells whether # starts a comment that runs to the end of its\n\t// line; when false it is an ordinary character.\n\tComments bool\n\n\t// Syntax tells whether parsed links record how their IDs were written, in\n\t// Link.RawID. When false the parser reads a bare abstract syntax tree (AST\n\t// mode) and every RawID is nil. NewParser turns it on.\n\tSyntax bool\n\n\t// Internal state\n\tsource          string\n\ttext            string\n\tlines           []string\n\tlineOffsets     []int\n\tpos             int\n\tdepth           int\n\tindentStack     []int\n\tbaseIndentation *int\n}\n\n// NewParser creates a new Parser with default settings.\nfunc NewParser() *Parser {\n\treturn &Parser{\n\t\tMaxInputSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024, // 10MB\n\t\tMaxDepth:     DefaultMaxDepth,\n\t\tComments:     true,\n\t\tSyntax:       true,\n\t}\n}\n\n// internalLink is an internal representation during parsing.\ntype internalLink struct {\n\tid           *string\n\trawID        *string // the ID exactly as the document wrote it\n\tvalues       []*internalLink\n\tchildren     []*internalLink\n\tisIndentedID bool\n\t// A parenthesized group is parsed as a nested document, isNested tells an\n\t// empty group apart from a link that simply has no nested content.\n\tnested   []*internalLink\n\tisNested bool\n}\n\n// Parse parses Lino notation text into a slice of Link objects.\nfunc (p *Parser) Parse(input string) ([]*Link, error) {\n\t// Validate input type (Go handles this at compile time)\n\t// Validate input size\n\tif len(input) > p.MaxInputSize {\n\t\treturn nil, errors.New(\"input size exceeds maximum allowed size\")\n\t}\n\n\tif input == \"\" || strings.TrimSpace(input) == \"\" {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Comments are blanked rather than removed, so every byte keeps the\n\t// position it was written at.\n\tprepared := input\n\tif p.Comments {\n\t\tprepared = StripComments(input)\n\t}\n\n\tp.source = input\n\tp.text = prepared\n\tp.lines, p.lineOffsets = p.splitLinesRespectingQuotes(prepared)\n\tp.pos = 0\n\tp.depth = 0\n\tp.indentStack = []int{0}\n\tp.baseIndentation = nil\n\n\trawResult, err := p.parseRoot()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn p.transformResult(rawResult), nil\n}\n\n// parseRoot parses the prepared document, turning a refusal to nest any deeper\n// into the error it carries.\nfunc (p *Parser) parseRoot() (result []*internalLink, err error) {\n\tdefer func() {\n\t\tif recovered := recover(); recovered != nil {\n\t\t\tif literal, ok := recovered.(referenceLiteralError); ok {\n\t\t\t\tresult, err = nil, literal.err\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\trefusal, ok := recovered.(nestingTooDeep)\n\t\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\t\tpanic(recovered)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tresult, err = nil, refusal.err\n\t\t}\n\t}()\n\treturn p.parseDocument(), nil\n}\n\n// checkDepth refuses, for good, a level deeper than MaxDepth. offset is where\n// in the document the level that is one too deep opens.\nfunc (p *Parser) checkDepth(depth, offset int) {\n\tif depth <= p.MaxDepth {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\t// The error quotes the document as the caller wrote it rather than the\n\t// copy with its comments blanked; both have every byte at the same offset.\n\tpanic(nestingTooDeep{err: newNestingTooDeepError(p.source, offset, p.MaxDepth)})\n}\n\n// isSubstantiveBody reports whether a body written between an even run of\n// delimiters is substantive: it holds at least one visible character and does\n// not straddle a parenthesis. An even run can always be read as delimiter pairs\n// enclosing nothing, so the n-quote reading is only taken when it carries\n// something the pairs cannot.\nfunc isSubstantiveBody(content string) bool {\n\tdepth := 0\n\thasVisible := false\n\n\tfor _, c := range content {\n\t\tswitch c {\n\t\tcase '(':\n\t\t\tdepth++\n\t\tcase ')':\n\t\t\tdepth--\n\t\t\tif depth < 0 {\n\t\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif !unicode.IsSpace(c) {\n\t\t\thasVisible = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn hasVisible && depth == 0\n}\n\n// parseQuotedStringAt parses the delimited reference starting at start.\n//\n// Any number N of quotes opens and closes the string, 2*N quotes are an escaped\n// quote sequence. A run of an even number of delimiters that does not open a\n// reference with a substantive body is the empty reference: the shortest\n// reading, a bare delimiter pair enclosing nothing, wins over a longer n-quote\n// delimiter.\n//\n// It returns the decoded value and the position right after the closing quotes,\n// or ok == false when text does not start a delimited reference.\nfunc parseQuotedStringAt(text string, start int) (value string, end int, ok bool) {\n\tif start >= len(text) {\n\t\treturn \"\", 0, false\n\t}\n\n\tquoteChar := text[start]\n\tif quoteChar != '\"' && quoteChar != '\\'' && quoteChar != '`' {\n\t\treturn \"\", 0, false\n\t}\n\n\tquoteCount := 0\n\tpos := start\n\tfor pos < len(text) && text[pos] == quoteChar {\n\t\tquoteCount++\n\t\tpos++\n\t}\n\n\tisEvenRun := quoteCount%2 == 0\n\topenClose := strings.Repeat(string(quoteChar), quoteCount)\n\tescapeSeq := strings.Repeat(string(quoteChar), quoteCount*2)\n\tvar content strings.Builder\n\n\tfor pos < len(text) {\n\t\tif strings.HasPrefix(text[pos:], escapeSeq) {\n\t\t\tcontent.WriteString(openClose)\n\t\t\tpos += len(escapeSeq)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif strings.HasPrefix(text[pos:], openClose) {\n\t\t\tafterClose := pos + quoteCount\n\t\t\tif afterClose >= len(text) || text[afterClose] != quoteChar {\n\t\t\t\tbody := content.String()\n\t\t\t\tif isEvenRun && !isSubstantiveBody(body) {\n\t\t\t\t\treturn \"\", start + quoteCount, true\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\treturn body, afterClose, true\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tcontent.WriteByte(text[pos])\n\t\tpos++\n\t}\n\n\tif isEvenRun {\n\t\treturn \"\", start + quoteCount, true\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"\", 0, false\n}\n\n// skipQuotedString skips over the quoted string starting at start.\n// It returns the position right after the closing quotes, or -1 when text does\n// not start a terminated quoted string.\nfunc (p *Parser) skipQuotedString(text string, start int) int {\n\t_, end, ok := parseQuotedStringAt(text, start)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn -1\n\t}\n\treturn end\n}\n\n// findMatchingParen finds the parenthesis closing the one at start.\n// Quoted strings are skipped, so parentheses inside them are ignored.\n// It returns -1 when the group is not closed.\nfunc (p *Parser) findMatchingParen(text string, start int) int {\n\tdepth := 0\n\ti := start\n\n\tfor i < len(text) {\n\t\tchar := text[i]\n\t\tif char == '\"' || char == '\\'' || char == '`' {\n\t\t\tif end := p.skipQuotedString(text, i); end > i {\n\t\t\t\ti = end\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else if char == '(' {\n\t\t\tdepth++\n\t\t} else if char == ')' {\n\t\t\tdepth--\n\t\t\tif depth == 0 {\n\t\t\t\treturn i\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\n\treturn -1\n}\n\n// splitLinesRespectingQuotes splits text into lines while preserving newlines inside quotes\n// and handling multiline parenthesized expressions. It also returns the byte\n// offset in text each line starts at.\nfunc (p *Parser) splitLinesRespectingQuotes(text string) ([]string, []int) {\n\tvar lines []string\n\tvar offsets []int\n\tvar currentLine strings.Builder\n\tlineStart := 0\n\tparenDepth := 0\n\ti := 0\n\n\tfor i < len(text) {\n\t\tchar := text[i]\n\n\t\tif char == '\"' || char == '\\'' || char == '`' {\n\t\t\tif end := p.skipQuotedString(text, i); end > i {\n\t\t\t\t// A quoted string is opaque: newlines inside it are content\n\t\t\t\tcurrentLine.WriteString(text[i:end])\n\t\t\t\ti = end\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcurrentLine.WriteByte(char)\n\t\t} else if char == '(' {\n\t\t\tparenDepth++\n\t\t\tcurrentLine.WriteByte(char)\n\t\t} else if char == ')' {\n\t\t\tparenDepth--\n\t\t\tcurrentLine.WriteByte(char)\n\t\t} else if char == '\\n' {\n\t\t\tif parenDepth > 0 {\n\t\t\t\t// Inside unclosed parens: preserve the newline\n\t\t\t\tcurrentLine.WriteByte(char)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tlines = append(lines, currentLine.String())\n\t\t\t\toffsets = append(offsets, lineStart)\n\t\t\t\tcurrentLine.Reset()\n\t\t\t\tlineStart = i + 1\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcurrentLine.WriteByte(char)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\n\t// Add the last line if non-empty\n\tif currentLine.Len() > 0 {\n\t\tlines = append(lines, currentLine.String())\n\t\toffsets = append(offsets, lineStart)\n\t}\n\n\treturn lines, offsets\n}\n\nfunc (p *Parser) parseDocument() []*internalLink {\n\tp.pos = 0\n\tvar links []*internalLink\n\n\tfor p.pos < len(p.lines) {\n\t\tline := p.lines[p.pos]\n\t\tif strings.TrimSpace(line) != \"\" {\n\t\t\telement := p.parseElement(0)\n\t\t\tif element != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlinks = append(links, element)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn links\n}\n\nfunc (p *Parser) parseElement(currentIndent int) *internalLink {\n\tif p.pos >= len(p.lines) {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tline := p.lines[p.pos]\n\tlineOffset := p.lineOffsets[p.pos]\n\trawIndent := countLeadingSpaces(line)\n\n\t// Set base indentation from first content line\n\tif p.baseIndentation == nil && strings.TrimSpace(line) != \"\" {\n\t\tp.baseIndentation = &rawIndent\n\t}\n\n\t// Normalize indentation relative to base\n\tbase := 0\n\tif p.baseIndentation != nil {\n\t\tbase = *p.baseIndentation\n\t}\n\tindent := max(rawIndent-base, 0)\n\n\tif indent < currentIndent {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tcontent := strings.TrimSpace(line)\n\tif content == \"\" {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tcontentOffset := lineOffset + leadingSpaceLength(line)\n\tp.pos++\n\n\t// Try to parse the line\n\telement := p.parseLineContent(content, contentOffset)\n\t// Only a line that parsed counts, so a group too deep inside it is reported\n\t// at its own parenthesis, and trailing spaces are never taken for a line.\n\tp.checkDepth(p.depth, contentOffset)\n\n\t// Check for children (indented lines that follow). They are one level\n\t// deeper than this line, and the first of them sets the indentation the\n\t// rest have to keep.\n\tvar children []*internalLink\n\tchildIndent := -1\n\tp.depth++\n\n\tfor p.pos < len(p.lines) {\n\t\t// A line holding nothing does not close a block: the block goes on at\n\t\t// the next line that holds something. Blanking a comment leaves such a\n\t\t// line behind, so this is also what keeps a block together around a\n\t\t// comment written inside it.\n\t\tfollowing := p.pos\n\t\tfor following < len(p.lines) && strings.TrimSpace(p.lines[following]) == \"\" {\n\t\t\tfollowing++\n\t\t}\n\t\tif following >= len(p.lines) {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\n\t\trawNextIndent := countLeadingSpaces(p.lines[following])\n\t\tnextIndent := max(rawNextIndent-base, 0)\n\n\t\tif nextIndent <= indent {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\t// A line indented less than the first child closes this block: it\n\t\t// belongs to an enclosing one.\n\t\tif childIndent >= 0 && nextIndent < childIndent {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tif childIndent < 0 {\n\t\t\tchildIndent = nextIndent\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tp.pos = following\n\t\tchild := p.parseElement(childIndent)\n\t\tif child != nil {\n\t\t\tchildren = append(children, child)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tp.depth--\n\n\tif len(children) > 0 {\n\t\telement.children = children\n\t}\n\n\treturn element\n}\n\n// leadingSpaceLength is the number of bytes of white space s starts with.\nfunc leadingSpaceLength(s string) int {\n\treturn len(s) - len(strings.TrimLeftFunc(s, unicode.IsSpace))\n}\n\nfunc countLeadingSpaces(s string) int {\n\tcount := 0\n\tfor _, c := range s {\n\t\tif c == ' ' {\n\t\t\tcount++\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn count\n}\n\n// parseLineContent parses the content of one line; offset is where in the\n// document the content starts.\nfunc (p *Parser) parseLineContent(content string, offset int) *internalLink {\n\t// A whole parenthesized group: (id: values), (values) or a nested document\n\tif strings.HasPrefix(content, \"(\") && p.findMatchingParen(content, 0) == len(content)-1 {\n\t\treturn p.parseParenthesized(content[1:len(content)-1], offset)\n\t}\n\n\t// Try indented ID syntax: id:\n\tif strings.HasSuffix(content, \":\") {\n\t\tref, raw := p.extractReference(content[:len(content)-1], offset)\n\t\treturn &internalLink{id: &ref, rawID: raw, values: nil, isIndentedID: true}\n\t}\n\n\t// Try single-line link: id: values\n\tif colonPos := p.findColonOutsideQuotes(content); colonPos >= 0 {\n\t\tafterColon := content[colonPos+1:]\n\t\tvaluesPart := strings.TrimSpace(afterColon)\n\t\tref, raw := p.extractReference(content[:colonPos], offset)\n\t\tvalues := p.parseValues(valuesPart, offset+colonPos+1+leadingSpaceLength(afterColon))\n\t\treturn &internalLink{id: &ref, rawID: raw, values: values}\n\t}\n\n\t// Simple value list\n\tvalues := p.parseValues(content, offset)\n\treturn &internalLink{values: values}\n}\n\n// parseParenthesized parses the content of a parenthesized group.\n//\n// The group opens a nested context that starts fresh at indentation level zero\n// and follows exactly the rules used at the root of the document, so line breaks\n// separate links and indentation nests them. The group is one level deeper\n// than the line it is written on, and is refused when that is deeper than\n// MaxDepth; offset is where in the document its opening parenthesis is.\nfunc (p *Parser) parseParenthesized(inner string, offset int) *internalLink {\n\tp.checkDepth(p.depth+1, offset)\n\treturn &internalLink{nested: p.parseNestedDocument(inner, offset+1), isNested: true}\n}\n\n// parseNestedDocument parses the text of a parenthesized group as a document of\n// its own, whose lines are one level deeper than the line the group is written\n// on. offset is where in the document inner starts.\nfunc (p *Parser) parseNestedDocument(inner string, offset int) []*internalLink {\n\tsavedLines := p.lines\n\tsavedLineOffsets := p.lineOffsets\n\tsavedPos := p.pos\n\tsavedDepth := p.depth\n\tsavedBaseIndentation := p.baseIndentation\n\tsavedIndentStack := p.indentStack\n\n\tp.lines, p.lineOffsets = p.splitLinesRespectingQuotes(inner)\n\tfor index := range p.lineOffsets {\n\t\tp.lineOffsets[index] += offset\n\t}\n\tp.pos = 0\n\tp.depth = savedDepth + 1\n\tp.baseIndentation = nil\n\tp.indentStack = []int{0}\n\tnested := p.parseDocument()\n\n\tp.lines = savedLines\n\tp.lineOffsets = savedLineOffsets\n\tp.pos = savedPos\n\tp.depth = savedDepth\n\tp.baseIndentation = savedBaseIndentation\n\tp.indentStack = savedIndentStack\n\n\treturn nested\n}\n\n// findColonOutsideQuotes finds a colon that is not inside quotes or parentheses.\nfunc (p *Parser) findColonOutsideQuotes(text string) int {\n\tparenDepth := 0\n\ti := 0\n\n\tfor i < len(text) {\n\t\tchar := text[i]\n\t\tif char == '\"' || char == '\\'' || char == '`' {\n\t\t\tif end := p.skipQuotedString(text, i); end > i {\n\t\t\t\ti = end\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t} else if char == '(' {\n\t\t\tparenDepth++\n\t\t} else if char == ')' {\n\t\t\tparenDepth--\n\t\t} else if char == ':' && parenDepth == 0 {\n\t\t\treturn i\n\t\t}\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\n\treturn -1\n}\n\n// parseValues parses a space separated list of values; offset is where in the\n// document text starts.\nfunc (p *Parser) parseValues(text string, offset int) []*internalLink {\n\tif text == \"\" {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\tvar values []*internalLink\n\ti := 0\n\n\tfor i < len(text) {\n\t\t// Skip whitespace\n\t\tfor i < len(text) && isWhitespace(rune(text[i])) {\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\t}\n\t\tif i >= len(text) {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Try to extract the next value\n\t\tvalueEnd, valueText := p.extractNextValue(text, i)\n\t\tif valueText != \"\" && strings.TrimSpace(valueText) != \"\" {\n\t\t\tvalues = append(values, p.parseValue(valueText, offset+i))\n\t\t}\n\t\tif valueEnd == i {\n\t\t\t// No progress made - skip this character to avoid infinite loop\n\t\t\ti++\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\ti = valueEnd\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn values\n}\n\nfunc isWhitespace(c rune) bool {\n\treturn c == ' ' || c == '\\t' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r'\n}\n\nfunc (p *Parser) extractNextValue(text string, start int) (int, string) {\n\tif start >= len(text) {\n\t\treturn start, \"\"\n\t}\n\n\t// Check if this starts with a delimited reference (any N quotes, or a bare\n\t// delimiter pair standing for the empty reference)\n\tif _, end, ok := parseQuotedStringAt(text, start); ok {\n\t\treturn end, text[start:end]\n\t}\n\n\t// Check if this starts with a parenthesized expression\n\tif text[start] == '(' {\n\t\tif end := p.findMatchingParen(text, start); end >= 0 {\n\t\t\treturn end + 1, text[start : end+1]\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn len(text), text[start:]\n\t}\n\n\t// Regular value - read until space or end. A quote that does not open a\n\t// delimited reference is an ordinary character of a bare reference, as in\n\t// the grammar, so it does not carry the value past a space: ('x y) holds\n\t// the two references 'x and y.\n\ti := start\n\tfor i < len(text) && text[i] != ' ' {\n\t\ti++\n\t}\n\n\treturn i, text[start:i]\n}\n\n// parseValue parses one value; offset is where in the document it starts.\nfunc (p *Parser) parseValue(value string, offset int) *internalLink {\n\t// Nested link in parentheses\n\tif strings.HasPrefix(value, \"(\") && p.findMatchingParen(value, 0) == len(value)-1 {\n\t\treturn p.parseParenthesized(value[1:len(value)-1], offset)\n\t}\n\n\t// Simple reference\n\tref, raw := p.extractReference(value, offset)\n\treturn &internalLink{id: &ref, rawID: raw}\n}\n\n// extractReference reads the reference written in text, which starts at offset\n// in the document. It returns the reference's value and the text it was\n// written as, sliced from the document as the caller wrote it (comments\n// included), which has every byte at the same offset as the prepared copy.\nfunc (p *Parser) extractReference(text string, offset int) (string, *string) {\n\tleading := leadingSpaceLength(text)\n\ttext = strings.TrimSpace(text)\n\tstart := offset + leading\n\tif literalPrefix.MatchString(text) {\n\t\tvalue, err := DecodeReferenceLiteral(text)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\tpanic(referenceLiteralError{err})\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn value, p.rawReference(start, len(text))\n\t}\n\n\t// Try delimited references (any N quotes, or a bare delimiter pair)\n\tif value, end, ok := parseQuotedStringAt(text, 0); ok {\n\t\treturn value, p.rawReference(start, end)\n\t}\n\n\t// Unquoted\n\treturn text, p.rawReference(start, len(text))\n}\n\n// rawReference is the length bytes of the document as written from start: how\n// a reference was written.\nfunc (p *Parser) rawReference(start, length int) *string {\n\tend := start + length\n\tif start < 0 || end > len(p.source) {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\traw := p.source[start:end]\n\treturn &raw\n}\n\n// withRawID records on link how its ID was written, unless the parser reads a\n// bare abstract syntax tree or the link has no ID.\nfunc (p *Parser) withRawID(link *Link, item *internalLink) *Link {\n\tif p.Syntax && link.ID != nil && item.rawID != nil {\n\t\traw := *item.rawID\n\t\tlink.RawID = &raw\n\t}\n\treturn link\n}\n\nfunc (p *Parser) transformResult(rawResult []*internalLink) []*Link {\n\tvar links []*Link\n\n\tfor _, item := range rawResult {\n\t\tif item != nil {\n\t\t\tp.collectLinks(item, nil, &links)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn links\n}\n\nfunc (p *Parser) collectLinks(item *internalLink, parentPath []*Link, result *[]*Link) {\n\tif item == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tchildren := item.children\n\n\t// Special case: indented ID syntax (id: followed by children)\n\tif item.isIndentedID && item.id != nil && len(item.values) == 0 && len(children) > 0 {\n\t\tvar childValues []*Link\n\t\tfor _, child := range children {\n\t\t\tchildValues = append(childValues, p.transformIndentedValue(child))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tcurrentLink := p.withRawID(&Link{ID: item.id, Values: childValues}, item)\n\n\t\tif len(parentPath) == 0 {\n\t\t\t*result = append(*result, currentLink)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t*result = append(*result, p.combinePathElements(parentPath, currentLink))\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// Regular indented structure\n\tif len(children) > 0 {\n\t\tcurrentLink := p.transformLink(item)\n\n\t\t// Add the link combined with parent path\n\t\tif len(parentPath) == 0 {\n\t\t\t*result = append(*result, currentLink)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t*result = append(*result, p.combinePathElements(parentPath, currentLink))\n\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Process each child with this item in the path\n\t\tnewPath := append(parentPath, currentLink)\n\t\tfor _, child := range children {\n\t\t\tp.collectLinks(child, newPath, result)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\t// Leaf item or item with inline values\n\tcurrentLink := p.transformLink(item)\n\n\tif len(parentPath) == 0
