Closed issues on related topics: none.\n\n## Problem\n\nGitHub sometimes cannot hand out a hosted macOS runner. macOS arm64 is the usual case, and these runs carry the notice \"Due to capacity constraints, jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience longer queue times\". When that happens, GitHub gives up on the job with:\n\n> The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts\n\nThe job ends as \\`cancelled\\` (sometimes \\`failure\\`), with no steps and an empty \\`runner_name\\`. No code ran, but the template treats the result like a test failure:\n\n- the release gate below refuses to release\n- the terminal status gate reports a failing or overrun job\n- nothing reruns the job, so on a push to \\`main\\` the release is skipped until someone notices and clicks \"Re-run failed jobs\"\n\n## Reproducible example\n\nThe template's macOS matrix leg:\n\n\\`\\`\\`yaml\n${matrix}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nThe release gate that needs every leg to succeed:\n\n\\`\\`\\`yaml\n${gate}\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n\\`${gatescript}\\` classifies a non-success result only as a failure, or a cancellation only as \\`supersede\\` or \\`overrun\\` (\"No supersede accounts for these cancellations; timeout-minutes would otherwise leave the run grey\"). An infrastructure failure is therefore reported as if the code were at fault.\n\nNothing in \\`.github/workflows/\\` reruns failed jobs: a grep for \\`rerun\\`, \\`run_attempt\\`, \\`not acquired\\` and \\`workflow_run\\` returns nothing.\n\nEvidence:\n\n- links-notation run https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41477660740, job \\`kotlin / ios\\` (\\`runs-on: macos-26\\`):\n  - conclusion \\`cancelled\\`, 0 steps, \\`runner_name: \"\"\\`\n  - it waited from 16:07:31 to 16:44:51\n  - annotation \"The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts\"\n  - the push to \\`main\\` therefore produced no release\n${extra}\n\nSteps to reproduce: push to \\`main\\` while macOS hosted capacity is constrained. Alternatively, simulate it by pointing one matrix leg at an unavailable label for a test branch. The gate turns red and stays red until someone reruns it by hand.\n\n## Workaround\n\nOpen the run and choose \"Re-run failed jobs\", or run \\`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed --repo ${repo}\\`. Because \\`--failed\\` also reruns dependent jobs, the release and status gates are re-evaluated.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n1. Rerun only infrastructure failures automatically, at most twice. A job that ran steps and failed is never rerun.\n\n\\`\\`\\`diff\n+++ .github/workflows/rerun-infrastructure-failures.yml\n+name: Rerun infrastructure failures\n+\n+on:\n+  workflow_run:  # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers] -- no checkout, reads only numeric run ids\n+    workflows: [${wfs}]\n+    types: [completed]\n+\n+permissions:\n+  actions: write\n+\n+jobs:\n+  rerun:\n+    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' && github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt < 3\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n+    timeout-minutes: 5\n+    concurrency:\n+      group: rerun-\\${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}\n+      cancel-in-progress: false\n+    steps:\n+      - name: Rerun jobs that never got a runner\n+        env:\n+          GH_TOKEN: [REDACTED] github.token }}\n+          REPO: \\${{ github.repository }}\n+          RUN_ID: \\${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}\n+          ATTEMPT: \\${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt }}\n+        run: |\n+          set -euo pipefail\n+          # A job that was never acquired has no runner and no steps; a real failure has both.\n+          stuck=\"\\$(gh api \"repos/\\$REPO/actions/runs/\\$RUN_ID/attempts/\\$ATTEMPT/jobs?per_page=100\" --paginate \\\\\n+            --jq '.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == \"cancelled\" or .conclusion == \"failure\")\n+                    and (.runner_name // \"\") == \"\" and ((.steps // []) | length) == 0) | .name')\"\n+          if [ -z \"\\$stuck\" ]; then\n+            echo \"No runner-acquisition failures in attempt \\$ATTEMPT; leaving the run as it is.\"\n+            exit 0\n+          fi\n+          echo \"::warning title=Hosted runner not acquired::\\$(echo \"\\$stuck\" | paste -sd, -) (attempt \\$ATTEMPT); rerunning failed jobs\"\n+          gh run rerun \"\\$RUN_ID\" --failed --repo \"\\$REPO\"\n\\`\\`\\`\n\n2. Make the status gate name the cause. It should stay red, because nothing was tested, but say why:\n\n\\`\\`\\`diff\n+# Jobs GitHub never started (no runner, no steps) are infrastructure, not code.\n+report_unacquired_jobs() {\n+  [ -n \"\\${GH_TOKEN:[REDACTED]}\" ] && [ -n \"\\${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-}\" ] || return 0\n+  local names\n+  names=\"\\$(gh api \"repos/\\${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/\\${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/attempts/\\${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-1}/jobs?per_page=100\" --paginate \\\\\n+    --jq '.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == \"cancelled\" or .conclusion == \"failure\") and (.runner_name // \"\") == \"\" and ((.steps // []) | length) == 0) | .name' 2>/dev/null || true)\"\n+  [ -z \"\\${names}\" ] && return 0\n+  echo \"::error title=Hosted runner not acquired::\\$(join_names \"\\${names}\"). GitHub could not provide a runner; no code ran. rerun-infrastructure-failures.yml reruns these automatically.\"\n+}\n+report_unacquired_jobs\n\\`\\`\\`\n\nPass \\`GH_TOKEN: [REDACTED] github.token }}\\` to the pipeline-status step. Its default \\`actions: read\\` permission is enough to list jobs.\n\n3. Optional: if macOS coverage is not needed to release, run the macOS leg as a non-blocking signal. [2026-11-02T17:22:51.984Z] [INFO]           "content": "# The npm lock of `.github/actions/artifact` is never audited; two open advisories ship in the action bundle\n\nTarget repository: link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template (checked at HEAD 67cfe05). There were no open issues when this was drafted. Related closed issues:\n\n- #58 added continuous auditing for the resolved Python dependencies\n- #68 refined `audit_dependencies.py`\n\nNeither covers npm.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe template ships a JavaScript action with a committed `package-lock.json`. The action's `dist` bundle, built by `ncc`, runs in every artifact upload and download step.\n\nThe Security workflow audits only the Python surfaces, so an advisory against that lock is invisible to every scheduled run (CI/CD best practices, principle 15). Dependabot does see it, but the template has no `dependabot.yml` to turn the alert into a PR.\n\n## Reproducible example\n\n```yaml\n# .github/workflows/security.yml:19-37\n  dependency-audit:\n    name: Audit Resolved Python Dependencies\n    ...\n      - name: Audit pyproject.toml and docs/requirements.txt\n        run: python scripts/audit_dependencies.py\n```\n\n```python\n# scripts/audit_dependencies.py:20\nDEPENDENCY_SURFACES = (\"pyproject.toml\", \"docs/requirements.txt\")\n```\n\n```json\n// .github/actions/artifact/package.json\n\"dependencies\": { \"@actions/artifact\": \"6.3.1\", \"@actions/core\": \"3.0.1\", \"@actions/glob\": \"0.7.0\" },\n\"overrides\": { \"archiver-utils\": { \"glob\": \"13.0.6\" } }\n```\n\nThe action is used by `links.yml:127`, `security.yml:81`, `docs.yml:74,90`, `release.yml:431,615,905,933` and `workflows.yml:176,184,196,204`.\n\nOpen Dependabot alerts on `main`, created 2026-11-01:\n\n- #2 minimatch in `.github/actions/artifact/package-lock.json`, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 (medium), fixed in 11.0.1\n- #1 glob in `.github/actions/artifact/package-lock.json`, GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (medium), fixed in 14.0.2. The `glob` override pins 13.0.6, inside the vulnerable range `>= 9.0.0, <= 14.0.1`.\n\nThe next scheduled Security run, https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/41461412029 (2026-11-02), was green.\n\nlinks-notation has the same blind spot class: an npm lock with an open GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 alert next to a green audit (link-foundation/links-notation#377).\n\nSteps to reproduce: `cd .github/actions/artifact && npm audit --package-lock-only` lists both advisories. No workflow runs that command.\n\n## Workaround\n\nBump the override to `glob` 14.0.2 or later, update `minimatch`, run `npm run build`, and commit `dist`. The `workflows.yml:161-166` check requires a matching bundle.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n```diff\n   dependency-audit:\n     ...\n       - name: Audit pyproject.toml and docs/requirements.txt\n         run: python scripts/audit_dependencies.py\n+\n+      - name: Setup Node.js\n+        uses: actions/setup-node@v7\n+        with:\n+          node-version: 24\n+\n+      - name: Audit the artifact action's npm lock\n+        working-directory: .github/actions/artifact\n+        run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=moderate\n```\n\nThe level here can be `moderate`: the lock is small and fully under the template's control. Also add a `.github/dependabot.yml` with `npm` for `/.github/actions/artifact` and `github-actions` for `/`, using the weekly schedule and `cooldown: default-days: 7` that the cpp and csharp templates use.\n\nNote: a Dependabot npm PR for this directory will fail `workflows.yml:161-166` (\"Verify committed action bundle\") until `dist` is rebuilt, because Dependabot does not run `npm run build`. Either regenerate `dist` in a follow-up commit on Dependabot PRs (push with a non-`GITHUB_TOKEN` actor so CI reruns), or document that those PRs need a manual `npm run build` commit. links-notation hit exactly this with its generated parser (#377, D6).\n"

[2026-11-02T17:23:28.843Z] [INFO]           "content": "# No dependency audit or Dependabot for pom.xml: Maven dependencies and plugins are never checked for advisories or updates\n\nTarget repository: link-foundation/java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template (checked at HEAD f7d89a3). There were no open issues when this was drafted, and no earlier issue mentions auditing. Severity: low.\n\n## Problem\n\nCI/CD best practices, principle 15, says code scanning does not audit dependencies, and the audit has to run on a schedule. The java template has neither part.\n\n- There is no `security.yml` and no audit step.\n- There is no `.github/dependabot.yml`.\n- `dependabot_security_updates` is disabled in the repository settings.\n- The only scheduled job, `workflows.yml` (`cron: '0 8 * * 1'`), checks GitHub Action pins. It does not check `pom.xml`.\n\nAn advisory against a pinned Maven dependency or build plugin would never surface. All the other templates with a security workflow run a full-severity scheduled audit:\n\n| template | audit |\n|---|---|\n| rust | `cargo audit --deny warnings` |\n| php | `composer audit --locked --abandoned=fail` |\n| csharp | `NuGetAuditLevel=low` plus `scripts/audit-dependencies.mjs` |\n| cpp | `pip-audit` |\n\n## Reproducible example\n\n```xml\n<!-- pom.xml:42-53 -->\n        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>\n        <spotless.version>2.43.0</spotless.version>\n        <checkstyle.version>10.12.7</checkstyle.version>\n        <spotbugs.version>4.8.3.1</spotbugs.version>\n        <jacoco.version>0.8.11</jacoco.version>\n        <maven-surefire.version>3.2.5</maven-surefire.version>\n        <maven-compiler.version>3.12.1</maven-compiler.version>\n        <maven-jar.version>3.3.0</maven-jar.version>\n        <maven-source.version>3.3.0</maven-source.version>\n        <maven-javadoc.version>3.6.3</maven-javadoc.version>\n        <maven-enforcer.version>3.4.1</maven-enforcer.version>\n```\n\n`ls .github/workflows` gives only `release.yml` and `workflows.yml`. `grep -rniE 'audit|osv|dependency-check|dependency-review' .github scripts` finds only the action-pin regression test (`workflows.yml:27`).\n\nMost of these versions date from early 2024. Nothing in CI reports that, or any advisory published against them.\n\n## Workaround\n\nRun an audit locally: `osv-scanner scan source -r .`, or `mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check`. Run `mvn versions:display-dependency-updates versions:display-plugin-updates` for freshness.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n```diff\n+++ .github/workflows/security.yml\n+name: Security\n+on:\n+  push:\n+    branches: [main]\n+  pull_request:\n+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]\n+  schedule:\n+    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'\n+  workflow_dispatch:\n+permissions:\n+  contents: read\n+jobs:\n+  dependency-audit:\n+    name: Audit Maven dependencies (OSV)\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n+    timeout-minutes: 10\n+    concurrency:\n+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-dependency-audit\n+      cancel-in-progress: true\n+    steps:\n+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1\n+        with:\n+          persist-credentials: false\n+      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6.0.1\n+        with:\n+          distribution: temurin\n+          java-version: '21'\n+      - name: Audit resolved dependency tree (all severities)\n+        run: |\n+          mvn -B -q dependency:tree -DoutputType=text -DoutputFile=target/deps.txt\n+          # Pin the scanner by version like the other workflow tools; check-ci-dependencies.mjs can track it.\n+          curl -fsSL -o osv-scanner https://github.com/google/osv-scanner/releases/download/v2.2.2/osv-scanner_linux_amd64\n+          chmod +x osv-scanner\n+          ./osv-scanner scan source --lockfile pom.xml\n```\n\n```diff\n+++ .github/dependabot.yml\n+version: 2\n+updates:\n+  - package-ecosystem: maven\n+    directory: /\n+    schedule:\n+      interval: weekly\n+    cooldown:\n+      default-days: 7\n+  - package-ecosystem: github-actions\n+    directory: /\n+    schedule:\n+      interval: weekly\n+    cooldown:\n+      default-days: 7\n```\n\nThe template already keeps every plugin version in a property, and `requireMavenVersion` uses a range (`pom.xml:253-255`, `[3.8.0,)`). Dependabot can therefore bump plugins safely. links-notation's `java/pom.xml` used one literal `3.6.3` for both the enforcer plugin and `requireMavenVersion`, and a Dependabot bump changed both (link-foundation/links-notation PR #363). The template's layout avoids that. Keep it.\n\nPin the OSV-Scanner version to the current release at implementation time, and verify its checksum, as the other workflow tools do.\n"

Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n\n## Quality Enforcement Strategy\n\nThe templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:\n\n```\nDeveloper Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release\n├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass\n├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump\n└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update\n                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package\n                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)\n                          ├── check-file-line-limits\n                          ├── test-suites\n                          ├── test-execution\n                          ├── validate-docs\n                          └── docker-pr-check\n```\n\nEach layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.",

There were no open issues when this was drafted. Closed issues on related topics: none.\n\n## Problem\n\nGitHub sometimes cannot hand out a hosted macOS runner. macOS arm64 is the usual case, and these runs carry the notice \"Due to capacity constraints, jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience longer queue times\". When that happens, GitHub gives up on the job with:\n\n> The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts\n\nThe job ends as `cancelled` (sometimes `failure`), with no steps and an empty `runner_name`. No code ran, but the template treats the result like a test failure:\n\n- the release gate below refuses to release\n- the terminal status gate reports a failing or overrun job\n- nothing reruns the job, so on a push to `main` the release is skipped until someone notices and clicks \"Re-run failed jobs\"\n\n## Reproducible example\n\nThe template's macOS matrix leg:\n\n```yaml\n# .github/workflows/release.yml:325-329\n    strategy:\n      fail-fast: false\n      matrix:\n        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-15, windows-2025]\n        runtime: [node, bun, deno]\n# .github/workflows/example-app.yml:254-254\n    runs-on: macos-15\n```\n\nThe release gate that needs every leg to succeed:\n\n```yaml\n# .github/workflows/release.yml:548-558\n    # Use !cancelled() instead of always() so cancellation propagates correctly (hive-mind issue #1278)\n    # This is needed because lint/test jobs have a transitive dependency on changeset-check\n    if: |\n      !cancelled() &&\n      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&\n      github.event_name == 'push' &&\n      needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' &&\n      needs.lint.result == 'success' &&\n      needs.test.result == 'success' &&\n      !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&\n      !contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')\n```\n\n`scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh` classifies a non-success result only as a failure, or a cancellation only as `supersede` or `overrun` (\"No supersede accounts for these cancellations; timeout-minutes would otherwise leave the run grey\"). An infrastructure failure is therefore reported as if the code were at fault.\n\nNothing in `.github/workflows/` reruns failed jobs: a grep for `rerun`, `run_attempt`, `not acquired` and `workflow_run` returns nothing.\n\nEvidence:\n\n- links-notation run https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41477660740, job `kotlin / ios` (`runs-on: macos-26`):\n  - conclusion `cancelled`, 0 steps, `runner_name: \"\"`\n  - it waited from 16:07:31 to 16:44:51\n  - annotation \"The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts\"\n  - the push to `main` therefore produced no release\n- The template's own runs carry the capacity notice. For example, Example app run https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/actions/runs/41351093333 annotates \"Due to capacity constraints, jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience longer queue times.\"",

Searches for \"requireMavenVersion\", \"maven-enforcer-plugin\" and \"maven ... same version\" found nothing related.\n\n### Package ecosystem\n\nMaven\n\n### Package manager version\n\nMaven 3.6.3 (`.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties`), maven-enforcer-plugin 3.6.3 → 3.7.0\n\n### Language version\n\nJava 8 (the release target), JDK 21 build\n\n### Manifest location and content before the Dependabot update\n\n`java/pom.xml` in https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation (public). Trimmed:\n\n```xml\n<plugin>\n    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>\n    <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>\n    <version>3.6.3</version>\n    <executions>\n        <execution>\n            <id>require-maven</id>\n            <goals><goal>enforce</goal></goals>\n            <configuration>\n                <rules>\n                    <requireMavenVersion>\n                        <version>3.6.3</version>\n                    </requireMavenVersion>\n                </rules>\n            </configuration>\n        </execution>\n    </executions>\n</plugin>\n```\n\nThe plugin version and the minimum Maven version happened to be the same string.\n\n### dependabot.yml content\n\n```yaml\nversion: 2\nupdates:\n  - package-ecosystem: \"maven\"\n    directory: \"/java\"\n    schedule:\n      interval: \"daily\"\n```\n\n### Updated dependency\n\n`org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-enforcer-plugin` 3.6.3 → 3.7.0\n\n### What you expected to see, versus what you actually saw\n\nExpected: only the plugin's own `<version>` changes.\n\nActual: both `<version>3.6.3</version>` lines changed (pull request https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/363):\n\n```diff\n                 <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>\n-                <version>3.6.3</version>\n+                <version>3.7.0</version>\n@@\n                                 <requireMavenVersion>\n-                                    <version>3.6.3</version>\n+                                    <version>3.7.0</version>\n                                 </requireMavenVersion>\n```\n\nThe second change is not a dependency update. It silently raised the project's minimum Maven version from 3.6.3 to 3.7.0, a Maven release that does not exist. The build that tests the floor then failed with `Detected Maven Version: 3.6.3 is not in the allowed range [3.7.0,)` (https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41439729658).\n\n### Cause\n\n`Dependabot::Maven::FileUpdater#updated_file_declaration` (`maven/lib/dependabot/maven/file_updater.rb`, lines 327-334 at 253cba827e22be90403ce312990a1a4e89defd3e) replaces every occurrence of the old version in the whole declaration string:\n\n```ruby\nold_declaration.gsub(\n  /(?<=\\s|>)#{Regexp.quote(original_req_string)}(?=\\s|<)/,\n  T.must(requirement.requirement_string)\n)\n```\n\nFor a plugin, `DeclarationFinder#declaration_strings` returns the whole `<plugin>` node, including `<executions>` and `<configuration>`. So any value in the plugin's configuration that equals the old version is rewritten too: `requireMavenVersion`, `requireJavaVersion`, a `<target>`/`<release>`, a `<version>` of a tool the plugin downloads, and so on.\n\n### Native package manager behavior\n\n`mvn versions:use-latest-releases` / `versions:set-property` only change the plugin's `<version>` child.\n\n### Smallest manifest that reproduces the issue\n\n```xml\n<project xmlns=\"http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0\">\n  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>\n  <groupId>example</groupId>\n  <artifactId>repro</artifactId>\n  <version>1.0.0</version>\n  <build>\n    <plugins>\n      <plugin>\n        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>\n        <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>\n        <version>3.6.3</version>\n        <executions>\n          <execution>\n            <id>require-maven</id>\n            <goals><goal>enforce</goal></goals>\n            <configuration>\n              <rules>\n                <requireMavenVersion><version>3.6.3</version></requireMavenVersion>\n              </rules>\n            </configuration>\n          </execution>\n        </executions>\n      </plugin>\n    </plugins>\n  </build>\n</project>\n```\n\nA Dependabot version update for maven-enforcer-plugin changes both `3.6.3` literals.\n\n### Workaround\n\nWrite the configuration value so that it cannot equal a plugin version. The enforcer reads the range `[3.6.3,)` the same way as `3.6.3`, so links-notation now declares `<version>[3.6.3,)</version>` (https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/378). Moving the value into a `<properties>` entry with a different name also works.\n\n### Suggested fix\n\nOnly rewrite the version of the dependency itself: the direct `<version>` child of the `<plugin>`/`<dependency>`/`<extension>` node, or the property it references. For example, in `updated_file_declaration`, parse the declaration and change only that child:\n\n```ruby\ndef updated_file_declaration(old_declaration, previous_req, requirement)\n  original_req_string = T.must(previous_req.requirement_string)\n  # Only the declaration's own <version>: nested <configuration> values\n  # (requireMavenVersion, release, ...) can hold the same text.\n  own_version = %r{\\A(.*?<version>\\s*)#{Regexp.quote(original_req_string)}(\\s*</version>)}m\n  head = old_declaration[/\\A.*?(?=<(?:executions|configuration|dependencies)>|\\z)/m]\n  return old_declaration unless head&.match?(own_version)\n\n  old_declaration.sub(own_version) { \"#{Regexp.last_match(1)}#{requirement.requirement_string}#{Regexp.last_match(2)}\" }\nend\n```\n\nA spec with the pom above should assert that `requireMavenVersion` keeps `3.6.3`.\nEOF\ncat > dependabot-core-yarn-lock-without-package-json.md <<'EOF'\n# npm_and_yarn: security updates for a `yarn.lock` with no `package.json` beside it fail every time with `dependency_file_not_found`\n\n### Is there an existing issue for this?\n\n- [x] I have searched the existing issues. #10684 and #15590 report `dependency_file_not_found` for other reasons: a deleted `directories:` entry, and a transitive dependency next to a `package.json` that does exist.\n\n### Package ecosystem\n\nnpm_and_yarn (yarn classic, lockfile v1)\n\n### Package manager version\n\nyarn 1.22 lockfile, generated by the Kotlin Gradle plugin 2.x (`kotlinUpgradeYarnLock`)\n\n### Language version\n\nKotlin Multiplatform, `js()` target\n\n### Manifest location and content before the Dependabot update\n\n`kotlin/kotlin-js-store/yarn.lock` in https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation (public). Every security update job for those alerts then fails:\n\n```\nJob definition: {\"job\":{\"command\":\"security\", ... \"dependencies\":[\"minimatch\"], ... \"source\":{ ... \"directories\":[\"/kotlin/kotlin-js-store\"]}}}\nERROR <job_1674697167> Error during file fetching; aborting: /kotlin/kotlin-js-store/package.json not found\n| dependency_file_not_found | { \"message\": \"/kotlin/kotlin-js-store/package.json not found\" } |\n```\n\nRuns:\n\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41478063329 (minimatch)\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41478058464 (glob)\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41478058822 (diff)\n\nThe failure repeats on every run, and the alerts stay open with no explanation in the alert itself.\n\nWhat I expected, either:\n\n1. the lockfile alone gets updated: for yarn classic, re-resolve the vulnerable entries in `yarn.lock` within the ranges already recorded there; or\n2. the job ends with a specific, documented error (for example `dependency_file_not_supported` with the message \"yarn.lock has no package.json beside it; it is generated by another build tool, so raise the version there\") instead of a generic \"file not found\", and the alert says why no pull request can be opened.\n\n### Native package manager behavior\n\n`yarn install` needs a `package.json`. The Kotlin Gradle plugin regenerates the lockfile from `build/js/package.json`, with `resolutions` taken from `YarnRootExtension.resolution(...)`.\n\n### Smallest manifest that reproduces the issue\n\nA repository containing only `sub/yarn.lock`, with one locked package affected by an advisory:\n\n```\n# yarn lockfile v1\n\n\nminimatch@^9.0.4:\n  version \"9.0.5\"\n  resolved \"https://registry.yarnpkg.com/minimatch/-/minimatch-9.0.5.tgz\"\n```\n\nOnce the dependency graph raises the alert, the security update fails with `/sub/package.json not found`.\n\n### Workaround\n\nRaise the versions in the tool that generates the lock. In Kotlin, add `resolution(\"minimatch\", \"^11.0.4\")` to `YarnRootExtension`, then run `./gradlew rootPackageJson --rerun kotlinUpgradeYarnLock`. Audit the lockfile in CI with the registry's bulk advisory endpoint, as `npm audit` cannot read it either. links-notation does both in https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/378 (`scripts/ci/audit-yarn-lock.mjs`).\n\n### Suggested fix\n\nIn `NpmAndYarn::FileFetcher`, when the directory has a `yarn.lock` and no `package.json`, raise `Dependabot::DependencyFileNotSupported` with the message above instead of `DependencyFileNotFound`. The security update service can then report it on the alert, and stop treating the job as failed. A fuller fix would be a lockfile-only update path for yarn classic: rewrite the vulnerable entries within their recorded ranges, as `yarn upgrade <name>` does for a transitive dependency.\nEOF\nls",

Searches for \"requireMavenVersion\", \"maven-enforcer-plugin\" and \"maven ... same version\" found nothing related.\n\n### Package ecosystem\n\nMaven\n\n### Package manager version\n\nMaven 3.6.3 (`.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties`), maven-enforcer-plugin 3.6.3 → 3.7.0\n\n### Language version\n\nJava 8 (the release target), JDK 21 build\n\n### Manifest location and content before the Dependabot update\n\n`java/pom.xml` in https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation (public). Trimmed:\n\n```xml\n<plugin>\n    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>\n    <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>\n    <version>3.6.3</version>\n    <executions>\n        <execution>\n            <id>require-maven</id>\n            <goals><goal>enforce</goal></goals>\n            <configuration>\n                <rules>\n                    <requireMavenVersion>\n                        <version>3.6.3</version>\n                    </requireMavenVersion>\n                </rules>\n            </configuration>\n        </execution>\n    </executions>\n</plugin>\n```\n\nThe plugin version and the minimum Maven version happened to be the same string.\n\n### dependabot.yml content\n\n```yaml\nversion: 2\nupdates:\n  - package-ecosystem: \"maven\"\n    directory: \"/java\"\n    schedule:\n      interval: \"daily\"\n```\n\n### Updated dependency\n\n`org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-enforcer-plugin` 3.6.3 → 3.7.0\n\n### What you expected to see, versus what you actually saw\n\nExpected: only the plugin's own `<version>` changes.\n\nActual: both `<version>3.6.3</version>` lines changed (pull request https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/363):\n\n```diff\n                 <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>\n-                <version>3.6.3</version>\n+                <version>3.7.0</version>\n@@\n                                 <requireMavenVersion>\n-                                    <version>3.6.3</version>\n+                                    <version>3.7.0</version>\n                                 </requireMavenVersion>\n```\n\nThe second change is not a dependency update. It silently raised the project's minimum Maven version from 3.6.3 to 3.7.0, a Maven release that does not exist. The build that tests the floor then failed with `Detected Maven Version: 3.6.3 is not in the allowed range [3.7.0,)` (https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41439729658).\n\n### Cause\n\n`Dependabot::Maven::FileUpdater#updated_file_declaration` (`maven/lib/dependabot/maven/file_updater.rb`, lines 327-334 at 253cba827e22be90403ce312990a1a4e89defd3e) replaces every occurrence of the old version in the whole declaration string:\n\n```ruby\nold_declaration.gsub(\n  /(?<=\\s|>)#{Regexp.quote(original_req_string)}(?=\\s|<)/,\n  T.must(requirement.requirement_string)\n)\n```\n\nFor a plugin, `DeclarationFinder#declaration_strings` returns the whole `<plugin>` node, including `<executions>` and `<configuration>`. So any value in the plugin's configuration that equals the old version is rewritten too: `requireMavenVersion`, `requireJavaVersion`, a `<target>`/`<release>`, a `<version>` of a tool the plugin downloads, and so on.\n\n### Native package manager behavior\n\n`mvn versions:use-latest-releases` / `versions:set-property` only change the plugin's `<version>` child.\n\n### Smallest manifest that reproduces the issue\n\n```xml\n<project xmlns=\"http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0\">\n  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>\n  <groupId>example</groupId>\n  <artifactId>repro</artifactId>\n  <version>1.0.0</version>\n  <build>\n    <plugins>\n      <plugin>\n        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>\n        <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>\n        <version>3.6.3</version>\n        <executions>\n          <execution>\n            <id>require-maven</id>\n            <goals><goal>enforce</goal></goals>\n            <configuration>\n              <rules>\n                <requireMavenVersion><version>3.6.3</version></requireMavenVersion>\n              </rules>\n            </configuration>\n          </execution>\n        </executions>\n      </plugin>\n    </plugins>\n  </build>\n</project>\n```\n\nA Dependabot version update for maven-enforcer-plugin changes both `3.6.3` literals.\n\n### Workaround\n\nWrite the configuration value so that it cannot equal a plugin version. The enforcer reads the range `[3.6.3,)` the same way as `3.6.3`, so links-notation now declares `<version>[3.6.3,)</version>` (https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/378). Moving the value into a `<properties>` entry with a different name also works.\n\n### Suggested fix\n\nOnly rewrite the version of the dependency itself: the direct `<version>` child of the `<plugin>`/`<dependency>`/`<extension>` node, or the property it references. For example, in `updated_file_declaration`, parse the declaration and change only that child:\n\n```ruby\ndef updated_file_declaration(old_declaration, previous_req, requirement)\n  original_req_string = T.must(previous_req.requirement_string)\n  # Only the declaration's own <version>: nested <configuration> values\n  # (requireMavenVersion, release, ...) can hold the same text.\n  own_version = %r{\\A(.*?<version>\\s*)#{Regexp.quote(original_req_string)}(\\s*</version>)}m\n  head = old_declaration[/\\A.*?(?=<(?:executions|configuration|dependencies)>|\\z)/m]\n  return old_declaration unless head&.match?(own_version)\n\n  old_declaration.sub(own_version) { \"#{Regexp.last_match(1)}#{requirement.requirement_string}#{Regexp.last_match(2)}\" }\nend\n```\n\nA spec with the pom above should assert that `requireMavenVersion` keeps `3.6.3`.\nEOF\ncat > dependabot-core-yarn-lock-without-package-json.md <<'EOF'\n# npm_and_yarn: security updates for a `yarn.lock` with no `package.json` beside it fail every time with `dependency_file_not_found`\n\n### Is there an existing issue for this?\n\n- [x] I have searched the existing issues. #10684 and #15590 report `dependency_file_not_found` for other reasons: a deleted `directories:` entry, and a transitive dependency next to a `package.json` that does exist.\n\n### Package ecosystem\n\nnpm_and_yarn (yarn classic, lockfile v1)\n\n### Package manager version\n\nyarn 1.22 lockfile, generated by the Kotlin Gradle plugin 2.x (`kotlinUpgradeYarnLock`)\n\n### Language version\n\nKotlin Multiplatform, `js()` target\n\n### Manifest location and content before the Dependabot update\n\n`kotlin/kotlin-js-store/yarn.lock` in https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation (public). Kotlin Multiplatform keeps the lockfile of its JavaScript test toolchain (Mocha, Karma, webpack) in `kotlin-js-store/yarn.lock` and commits it, as JetBrains documents: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/js-project-setup.html#version-locking-via-kotlin-js-store. The matching `package.json` is generated at build time under `build/js/` and is not committed. The directory holds only the lockfile.\n\n### dependabot.yml content\n\nThe directory is not configured in `dependabot.yml`. The jobs below are the security updates GitHub starts for the alerts the dependency graph raises on that lockfile.\n\n### Updated dependency\n\nminimatch (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), glob (GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4), diff (GHSA-73rr-hh4g-fpgx)\n\n### What you expected to see, versus what you actually saw\n\nThe dependency graph reads the lockfile and raises Dependabot alerts on it. Every security update job for those alerts then fails:\n\n```\nJob definition: {\"job\":{\"command\":\"security\", ... \"dependencies\":[\"minimatch\"], ... \"source\":{ ... \"directories\":[\"/kotlin/kotlin-js-store\"]}}}\nERROR <job_1674697167> Error during file fetching; aborting: /kotlin/kotlin-js-store/package.json not found\n| dependency_file_not_found | { \"message\": \"/kotlin/kotlin-js-store/package.json not found\" } |\n```\n\nRuns:\n\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41478063329 (minimatch)\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41478058464 (glob)\n- https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/actions/runs/41478058822 (diff)\n\nThe failure repeats on every run, and the alerts stay open with no explanation in the alert itself.\n\nWhat I expected, either:\n\n1. the lockfile alone gets updated: for yarn classic, re-resolve the vulnerable entries in `yarn.lock` within the ranges already recorded there; or\n2. the job ends with a specific, documented error (for example `dependency_file_not_supported` with the message \"yarn.lock has no package.json beside it; it is generated by another build tool, so raise the version there\") instead of a generic \"file not found\", and the alert says why no pull request can be opened.\n\n### Native package manager behavior\n\n`yarn install` needs a `package.json`. The Kotlin Gradle plugin regenerates the lockfile from `build/js/package.json`, with `resolutions` taken from `YarnRootExtension.resolution(...)`.\n\n### Smallest manifest that reproduces the issue\n\nA repository containing only `sub/yarn.lock`, with one locked package affected by an advisory:\n\n```\n# yarn lockfile v1\n\n\nminimatch@^9.0.4:\n  version \"9.0.5\"\n  resolved \"https://registry.yarnpkg.com/minimatch/-/minimatch-9.0.5.tgz\"\n```\n\nOnce the dependency graph raises the alert, the security update fails with `/sub/package.json not found`.\n\n### Workaround\n\nRaise the versions in the tool that generates the lock. In Kotlin, add `resolution(\"minimatch\", \"^11.0.4\")` to `YarnRootExtension`, then run `./gradlew rootPackageJson --rerun kotlinUpgradeYarnLock`. Audit the lockfile in CI with the registry's bulk advisory endpoint, as `npm audit` cannot read it either. links-notation does both in https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/378 (`scripts/ci/audit-yarn-lock.mjs`).\n\n### Suggested fix\n\nIn `NpmAndYarn::FileFetcher`, when the directory has a `yarn.lock` and no `package.json`, raise `Dependabot::DependencyFileNotSupported` with the message above instead of `DependencyFileNotFound`. The security update service can then report it on the alert, and stop treating the job as failed. A fuller fix would be a lockfile-only update path for yarn classic: rewrite the vulnerable entries within their recorded ranges, as `yarn upgrade <name>` does for a transitive dependency.\nEOF\nls",

[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+### Suggested fix",
[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+In `NpmAndYarn::FileFetcher`, when the directory has a `yarn.lock` and no `package.json`, raise `Dependabot::DependencyFileNotSupported` with the message above instead of `DependencyFileNotFound`. [2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+",

[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+```ruby",

[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+  original_req_string = T.must(previous_req.requirement_string)",
[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+  # Only the declaration's own <version>: nested <configuration> values",

[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+",
[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+  old_declaration.sub(own_version) { \"#{Regexp.last_match(1)}#{requirement.requirement_string}#{Regexp.last_match(2)}\" }",

[2026-11-02T18:03:43.774Z] [INFO]                 "+",

In a Kotlin Multiplatform project with a `js()` target, run `./gradlew kotlinUpgradeYarnLock` and commit `kotlin-js-store/yarn.lock`.\n2. Add a resolution for a transitive dependency of the test toolchain, for example:\n\n   ```kotlin\n   plugins.withType<org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.js.yarn.YarnPlugin> {\n       the<org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.js.yarn.YarnRootExtension>().apply {\n           resolution(\"minimatch\", \"^11.0.4\")\n       }\n   }\n   ```\n3. The [upgrading guide section](https://docs.gradle.org/9.8.2/userguide/upgrading_version_9.html#kgp_native_bundle_attribute_enum) and the Javadoc of `AttributeTypeValidator.isKGPSpecialCase` make the same claim: \"KGP 2.1.0+ no longer uses this enum\".\n\nStack trace (`-Dorg.gradle.deprecation.trace=true`, KGP 2.4.21):\n\n```\nat org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.native.toolchain.KotlinNativeBundleArtifactFormat.<clinit>(KotlinNativeBundleArtifactFormat.kt:25)\nat org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.native.internal.CommonizerTasksKt.getCommonizeNativeDistributionTask(CommonizerTasks.kt:187)\nat org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.native.internal.CommonizerTasksKt.commonizedNativeDistributionKlibsOrNull(CommonizerTasks.kt:170)\nat org.jetbrains.kotlin.gradle.targets.native.internal.SetupKotlinNativePlatformDependenciesAndStdlibKt.getNativeDistributionDependencies(SetupKotlinNativePlatformDependenciesAndStdlib.kt:107)\n```\n\n### Expected Behavior\n\nThe message and the upgrading guide name the first KGP release that is unaffected, KGP 2.5.0. Until that release is stable, they should say that no stable KGP avoids the warning, so users do not chase an upgrade that does not help.\n\n### Context (optional)\n\nFound in the CI of https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation (issue https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/issues/377). Every Kotlin job ends with \"Deprecated Gradle features were used in this build, making it incompatible with Gradle 10\", and this is the only deprecation behind it.\n\n**Workaround:** none on stable KGP; the warning can only be left in place. KGP 2.5.0-Beta2 has no warning: the same reproducer with `version \"2.5.0-Beta2\"` prints no deprecation.\n\n**Suggested fix:** in `AttributeTypeValidator` (the Javadoc of `KGP_NATIVE_BUNDLE_ENUM_FQN` and `isKGPSpecialCase`), in the deprecation message, and in `upgrading_version_9.adoc#kgp_native_bundle_attribute_enum`, replace \"the Kotlin Gradle Plugin 2.0.x line … upgrade to KGP 2.1.0 or later\" with \"Kotlin Gradle Plugin versions before 2.5.0 (KT-89265) … upgrade to KGP 2.5.0 or later\". [2026-11-02T18:15:24.679Z] [INFO]         "content": "## Key CI/CD Principles\n\n> **Pin hosted runner operating systems.** Mutable aliases such as\n> `ubuntu-latest` can switch major OS versions without a repository diff and\n> emit migration notices. Use an explicit supported label such as\n> `ubuntu-24.04`, then upgrade in a dedicated compatibility PR.\n\n### 1. Run Checks Only on Relevant File Changes\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n\n## Quality Enforcement Strategy\n# Template comparison for issue #377 (snapshot 2026-11-02)\n\nCompared: `link-foundation/<lang>-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` (snapshots in\n`templates/<lang>/`) against this repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml`,\n`.github/dependabot.yml`, `scripts/` and `scripts/ci/`. Use an explicit supported label such as\n> `ubuntu-24.04`, then upgrade in a dedicated compatibility PR.\n\n### 1. Run Checks Only on Relevant File Changes\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. File Size Limits\n\n**Enforce a maximum of 1000-1500 lines per code file.**\n\nThis constraint benefits both AI and human developers:\n\n- AI models can read and understand entire files within context windows\n- Humans can navigate and comprehend files without cognitive overload\n- Forces modular, well-organized code architecture\n\nExample enforcement in CI (bash):\n\n```bash\nfind src/ -name \"*.mjs\" -type f | while read -r file; do\n  line_count=$(wc -l < \"$file\")\n  if [ \"$line_count\" -gt 1500 ]; then\n    echo \"ERROR: $file has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)\"\n    echo \"::error file=$file::File has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)\"\n    exit 1\n  fi\ndone\n```\n\n**Synchronize the file-size ESLint rule with the CI check** to catch violations locally before CI:\n\n```js\n// eslint.config.mjs\n{\n  rules: {\n    'max-lines': ['error', { max: 1500 }]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 7. Validate the Actual Merge Result\n\n**CI must test what will actually be merged, not a stale PR snapshot.**\n\nWhen a PR is opened against a base branch that later receives new commits, the GitHub merge preview can become stale. Simulate a fresh merge before running checks:\n\n```yaml\n- name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)\n  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n  env:\n    BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}\n  run: |\n    git config user.email \"github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com\"\n    git config user.name \"github-actions[bot]\"\n    git fetch origin \"$BASE_REF\"\n    BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)\n    if [ \"$BEHIND_COUNT\" -gt 0 ]; then\n      git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit || \\\n        (echo \"::error::Merge conflict! PR must be rebased before merging.\" && exit 1)\n    fi\n```\n\nThis ensures lint, file-size, and other checks validate the final merged state.\n\n### 13. Container Images: Native Runners per Architecture\n\n**Build each architecture on its own native runner.** GitHub provides free arm64 Linux runners for public repositories (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`). Emulating arm64 with QEMU on an x86 runner is much slower for compiled languages, and building two architectures inside one job makes them sequential instead of parallel.\n\n```yaml\nbuild-image:\n  strategy:\n    matrix:\n      include:\n        - platform: linux/amd64\n          runner: ubuntu-24.04\n        - platform: linux/arm64\n          runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. File Size Limits\n\n**Enforce a maximum of 1000-1500 lines per code file.**\n\nThis constraint benefits both AI and human developers:\n\n- AI models can read and understand entire files within context windows\n- Humans can navigate and comprehend files without cognitive overload\n- Forces modular, well-organized code architecture\n\nExample enforcement in CI (bash):\n\n```bash\nfind src/ -name \"*.mjs\" -type f | while read -r file; do\n  line_count=$(wc -l < \"$file\")\n  if [ \"$line_count\" -gt 1500 ]; then\n    echo \"ERROR: $file has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)\"\n    echo \"::error file=$file::File has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)\"\n    exit 1\n  fi\ndone\n```\n\n**Synchronize the file-size ESLint rule with the CI check** to catch violations locally before CI:\n\n```js\n// eslint.config.mjs\n{\n  rules: {\n    'max-lines': ['error', { max: 1500 }]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### 7. Emulating arm64 with QEMU on an x86 runner is much slower for compiled languages, and building two architectures inside one job makes them sequential instead of parallel.\n\n```yaml\nbuild-image:\n  strategy:\n    matrix:\n      include:\n        - platform: linux/amd64\n          runner: ubuntu-24.04\n        - platform: linux/arm64\n          runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. A `StreamParser` cut a document at a line that leaves a quote run open\n\n- **Evidence:** found while fixing A1. The stream gave a different result from the whole-document\n  parse for `a \"\" b` followed by `\"\" c`.\n- **Root cause:** the stream decided that a line was complete by counting quote characters one at a\n  time. It ignored that `\"\"` is an empty reference, so a line with an even run of quotes was\n  treated as unterminated, or as terminated, the wrong way round.\n- **Fix:** the stream now waits for the line that closes an even run of quotes:\n  - in JS, `a875202`;\n  - in the ports, in the same commits as A1.\n- **Verified:** there is a regression test in each binding that compares the stream with the\n  whole-document parse.\n\n### A3. The generated parser went stale on a peggy update\n\n- **Evidence:** CI 41478085102 on Dependabot's peggy 5.1.1 pull request, `js / test`. The step\n  `git diff --exit-code -- src/parser-generated.js` failed, and it printed only a bare diff.\n- **Root cause:**\n  - `js/src/parser-generated.js` is committed, and peggy 5.1.1 generates slightly different code.\n  - The gate was right to fail, but it did not say why or what to run.\n- **Fix (`478a505`):**\n  - The parser is regenerated with peggy 5.1.1.\n  - The gate now names the peggy version and the command\n    (`bun run build:grammar` / `npm run build:grammar`).\n- **Verified:** `js / test` regenerates the parser and diffs it. Locally, the diff is empty.\n\n### A4. A Dependabot plugin bump raised the Maven floor\n\n- **Evidence:**\n  - CI 41439729658 on PR #363 (maven-enforcer-plugin 3.6.3 → 3.7.0), `java / maven-floor`:\n    `Detected Maven Version: 3.6.3 is not in the allowed range [3.7.0,).`\n  - The diff is in `../pr/dependabot-363.diff`.\n- **Root cause:**\n  - `requireMavenVersion` held the literal `3.6.3`, which was also the enforcer plugin's version.\n  - Dependabot's Maven updater rewrites every occurrence of the old version string in the\n    plugin's `<configuration>`, so it also raised the floor.\n- **Fix (`07e6f64`):**\n  - The floor is written as the range `[3.6.3,)`, a string that Dependabot does not rewrite.\n  - `maven-floor` checks that the declared floor matches the Maven version it installs.\n- **Upstream:** dependabot-core#16797.\n- **Verified:** `experiments/issue-377` reproduces the rewrite, and the `maven-floor` job passes.\n\n### A5. Dependabot cannot update the Kotlin/JS `yarn.lock`\n\n- **Evidence:**\n  - Dependabot runs 41478058464, 41478058822 and 41478063329 (the minimatch security update)\n    failed with:\n    `Error during file fetching; aborting: /kotlin/kotlin-js-store/package.json not found`.\n  - `../ci-logs/dependabot-alerts-open.tsv` lists open alerts for diff, glob and minimatch against\n    that lock.\n- **Root cause:**\n  - Kotlin Multiplatform writes `kotlin/kotlin-js-store/yarn.lock` with no `package.json` next to\n    it. The `package.json` is generated under `build/js` at build time.\n  - Dependabot's npm/yarn updater requires a manifest, so these alerts can never be fixed\n    automatically.\n  - Nothing in CI audited this lock either; see C6.\n- **Fix:**\n  - `3c113f8` adds `yarn.resolutions` for diff, glob and minimatch, set in `kotlin/build.gradle.kts`\n    through `rootProject.extensions.configure<YarnRootExtension>` and regenerated with\n    `kotlinUpgradeYarnLock`.\n  - `cc23a71` audits the lock (C6).\n- **Upstream:**\n  - dependabot-core#16798.\n  - A Kotlin YouTrack report about `rootPackageJson` ignoring resolutions is **blocked**: JetBrains/kotlin\n    has GitHub issues disabled, and YouTrack needs an account. The draft is in\n    `../upstream/third-party/`.\n- **Verified:** `kotlin/kotlin-js-store/yarn.lock` resolves the fixed versions, and the yarn.lock\n  audit passes.\n\n### A6. A hosted macOS runner was never acquired\n\n- **Evidence:**\n  - CI 41477660740, `kotlin / ios` on `macos-26`, was cancelled after 37 minutes with\n    `The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts`.\n  - It ran no steps, and its `runner_name` is empty (`../ci-logs/CI-41477660740-kotlin-ios-job.json`).\n  - As a result, `release` was skipped.\n- **Root cause:** a GitHub-hosted capacity shortage. The same runs carry 12 notices\n  \"Due to capacity constraints, jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience longer queue\n  times\". No commit can fix this, so a re-run is the remedy.\n- **Fix (`a40a1f3`):**\n  - `rerun-unacquired.yml` starts on `workflow_run` completion.\n  - It re-runs the failed jobs once, only when every failed job ran no steps and has no runner\n    name.\n  - Any other failure is left alone.\n- **Upstream:** the same gap is reported to the templates that use hosted macOS or Windows\n  runners (`../upstream/URLS.txt`, \"runner-acquisition-rerun\").\n\n## B.
